intro: Wireless communication, RF heating and source-specific health research, with their different exposure conditions kept visible.

paragraphs.text: A useful RF exposure description follows a chain from the transmitter to the body. Frequency identifies the part of the spectrum; the device’s power and traffic describe its output; an instrument describes the field at a location; and dosimetry estimates energy absorbed in tissue. Those are related quantities, with different units and assumptions. The WLAN measurement papers illustrate a further distinction: device radiation patterns and the fraction of time transmitting affect how maximum-output tests relate to ordinary activity. A reported peak beside an access point therefore cannot be substituted directly for an occupied-room average or a person’s absorbed dose. Check the quantity, position, operating state and averaging period before comparing two reports.

The household survey measured selected smart-meter modules, cordless systems, baby monitors and Bluetooth peripherals. Its value lies in identifying actual devices, positions and operating states, rather than treating a home as having one uniform RF exposure. Its convenience sample also limits generalisation: a measured peak and a transmission duty factor describe the tested scenario, with no assurance that every current product behaves the same way. The Bluetooth measurements make this concrete. A mouse or speaker attempting to pair is a different source arrangement from an earbud streaming at the ear. For a reader comparing devices, the most useful question is which complete arrangement was tested, including the active radios, body position and task.

RF energy can be absorbed and produce heating; ICNIRP’s assessment connects that interaction to the exposed tissue, duration and dose quantity. A proposed explanation for a low-level disease association needs additional evidence that the relevant steps occur under the exposure in question. Endpoints help distinguish these claims. A sleep EEG feature measures electrical activity, a memory task measures performance, an isolated-sperm assay measures a laboratory response, and a tumour diagnosis is a clinical outcome. They cannot be pooled as interchangeable instances of damage. The Wi-Fi memory report itself calls its declarative-memory result inconclusive when considered with its other findings. A physiological or statistical difference can be worth investigating without establishing improved cognition, injury or a disease mechanism.

Basic restrictions address relevant quantities within the body, while external reference levels support practical exposure assessment under specified conditions. Neither is the same as a category chosen to analyse an observational study. This matters when a headline calls a study’s highest-use group a safety threshold: that group may reflect the available questionnaire or statistical design, rather than a boundary established by an exposure guideline. Product rules have another scope. The FDA’s microwave-oven framework concerns a US appliance-performance setting, including the enclosure and interlocks; it does not supply one limit for every wireless source or chronic outcome. Compare the correct quantity, frequency, body region and averaging rule, then distinguish that technical comparison from a health-effect estimate.

modules.label: Distance

paragraphs.text: Distance changes the relationship between an emitting source and the body, but a useful comparison also holds track of the device’s activity. FOPH describes phone exposure as depending on connection quality, use and position, and WLAN exposure as depending on traffic and transmission conditions. Moving a handset while its output changes is therefore a different comparison from measuring a fixed access point under a defined load. A single distance, technology name or maximum rating cannot reconstruct either scenario. Source-specific measurements or models can describe an exposure change if their operating assumptions are clear. Demonstrating that the change improves sleep or prevents a disease would require a separate outcome comparison, rather than being inferred from the lower exposure alone.

modules.title: Distance works with geometry and behavior

modules.label: Evidence

paragraphs.text: Start with the health outcome and the comparison that could answer it. Prospective phone cohorts and retrospective case-control studies address tumour incidence using different exposure histories and sources of bias; animal experiments contribute a separate stream. Acute sham-controlled symptom studies address a short-term trigger under their tested signals and observation windows. A Wi-Fi experiment cannot be replaced by a phone study simply because both involve RF, and a measured emissions survey adds no new disease cases. The linked outcome pages keep those contrasts identifiable, including conflicting findings, overlapping reports and missing full texts. This selection supplies no pooled RF risk or formal certainty grade; its usefulness comes from showing which result belongs to which exposure and outcome.

A radiofrequency field recorded inside a vehicle can include signals from cellular networks and passenger phones. The electric-bus survey separated selected RF bands and found cellular contributions; it did not isolate the vehicle battery or motor as the cause of every onboard RF reading. These environmental measurements are distinct from absorbed dose, clinical outcomes and a vehicle-wide safety conclusion.

modules.title: Follow the source and the endpoint

overview.text: Radiofrequency sources include mobile and cordless phones, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, transmitters and microwave ovens. Their shared physical category does not make a handset against the head equivalent to an access point across a room or energy contained in a cooking cavity. Start by naming the emitting component and the person’s position before interpreting a measurement.

The research here spans human cohorts, acute sham-controlled experiments, animal bioassays and device measurements. Each supplies a different comparison. A measured emission is useful exposure information; it is not an additional human health study. Several reports may also describe the same participants.

takeaway: Frequency identifies a field category. It does not specify dose, operating state, tissue exposure or a health outcome.

intro: Electrical power systems, occupational tasks and residential magnetic-field research.

paragraphs.text: Power-system exposure needs more than the name of an appliance. The electric field, magnetic field and internal induced field are different quantities, even when they arise around the same installation. A description should specify the component, frequency, location and observation period before presenting a magnitude. The epidemiological literature introduces another layer: wire codes and residential distance are ways of classifying an exposure setting, rather than direct readings of each person’s daily field. An instrument measurement may be more specific to a place and time while still missing past residence or activity elsewhere. Keeping these definitions visible helps explain why two studies can investigate low-frequency fields yet compare different variables and have different exposure errors.

Residential and occupational questions need different exposure histories. A birth address near a transmission line, a wiring category and a spot measurement in a room each describe part of a residential setting; none automatically captures a child’s complete exposure over years. A workplace assessment instead starts with equipment, tasks and the circumstances of workers who may be particularly susceptible. HSE’s UK framework uses available equipment and emission information, with measurement or modelling where that information is insufficient. These purposes should remain separate when comparing research: an address-based childhood study does not audit a current workstation, and an occupational assessment does not estimate the long-term exposure of every resident near a power line.

At sufficient low-frequency exposure, induced internal electric fields can stimulate excitable tissue. That established interaction is different from explaining the observational childhood-leukaemia association. Evidence for a mechanism would need to connect the relevant exposure to a causal process for that particular outcome, rather than treating stimulation as proof of all chronic effects. The pooled leukaemia analyses retain an association in higher exposure categories, while selection, confounding and exposure-history error complicate interpretation. Both statements belong in the account. The association should not disappear because its cause remains uncertain, but neither can it be converted into a causal estimate for a particular child or a prediction from one household meter reading.

An epidemiological category, a guideline value and an appliance measurement have different jobs. Categories in pooled childhood-leukaemia analyses group the observations available for comparison; they do not establish a residential exclusion zone or a clinically validated safe reading. Guidance addresses specified exposure interactions and assessment conditions. Appliance-use reports add another limitation: historical electric-blanket use is a product and behaviour proxy, with no guarantee that the same information describes current wiring, settings or overnight operation. The recovered review treats appliance-use and measured residential-field analyses separately for that reason. A useful interpretation identifies the quantity and exposure history first, then explains what the comparison can say about its own outcome.

modules.label: Distance

paragraphs.text: A geographical distance study can compare many addresses without measuring every field at those addresses. That makes it useful for investigating a location-based hypothesis, but leaves the relationship with personal magnetic-field exposure uncertain. Other electrical sources, the line’s configuration and a person’s residence and activity history can alter that relationship. The power-line pregnancy and fertility reports therefore need their own exposure descriptions. In the infertility case-control paper, proximity was reported rather than individual dose being measured, and unresolved table counts keep numerical claims held. A distance association does not establish which source caused it or provide an evidence-based relocation rule. Those would require more complete exposure and causal information than the distance variable supplies.

modules.title: A proxy is not a dosimeter

paragraphs.text: The childhood-leukaemia pooled analyses reuse overlapping underlying studies. Their agreement or disagreement should be assessed through inclusion rules, populations and exposure methods, rather than by counting each publication as an independent replication. Draper’s distance study asks a related geographical question with a different exposure definition. Occupational meningioma and residential pregnancy reports then address different populations and endpoints again. Preserving those distinctions makes a comparison table more informative than a single ELF verdict: a result about one diagnosis and proxy cannot settle every outcome associated with electrical systems. The source records show the actual designs and outstanding inputs, while the outcome pages explain where findings are consistent, mixed or too incompletely assessed for a stronger interpretation.

A negative cell experiment is informative when its exposure and methods are clear, but its scope still matters. Luceri and colleagues measured DNA-damage markers in isolated lymphocytes and gene expression in both lymphocytes and yeast. The final analyses did not support an exposure-related effect in those assays. Some initially highlighted gene changes disappeared under the final statistical methods, illustrating why a preliminary list should not replace the completed analysis. At the same time, pooled donor samples, limited independent replication and culture-setting differences restrict what the result can exclude. It does not directly measure disease risk or settle every possible response to ELF magnetic fields.

overview.text: Power lines, wiring and appliances produce low-frequency fields associated with electrical systems. The ICNIRP low-frequency material describes common power frequencies and the interaction of induced internal fields with the nervous system. Electric and magnetic components require their own quantities and measurement context.

The best-developed selected health comparison here is childhood leukaemia and residential magnetic fields. The higher categories in pooled observational analyses were associated with elevated estimates, but causation remains unresolved. Neither a category boundary nor a distance from a line is a demonstrated threshold at which disease begins.

takeaway: Electric and magnetic fields, measured exposure and distance proxies must remain distinct.
title: Power-frequency and ELF fields

intro: Induction systems and mixed electrical technologies need component-specific exposure descriptions.

paragraphs.text: Induction cooking is an energy-transfer system comprising the hob, suitable pan and their relative positions. The field heats the pan through induced currents and magnetisation, while some field remains outside it. A selected power setting alone does not specify the field at a person’s body; pan size, alignment and position are part of the exposure arrangement. The same component-based approach is useful for vehicles and chargers. The recovered DC-charger paper models a transformer-related component in a defined geometry, with anatomical representations used for dosimetry. Its model does not inventory every motor, cable, cabin or charging source. Establishing which component was assessed prevents a precise calculation being mistaken for a complete assessment of a whole product.

The household induction model estimates exposure at a defined cooking position from information such as distance, cookware and operating power. That is useful for making exposure assignment more feasible in research, but it is different from following a person as they move, change settings and spend varying time at the hob. A fixed-position estimate can only represent the daily activity to the extent that its assumptions match that activity. FOPH’s cookware and placement guidance supplies source-specific context, with no direct pregnancy-benefit trial. When comparing households, retain both the appliance configuration and the duration or behaviour information that the model does not fully observe; a single cooker-use label loses much of that distinction.

Exposure assessment often proceeds from an external magnetic field to an estimate of an internal induced quantity. These are different stages of a model, with assumptions about source geometry, position and the body. An external comparison alone therefore cannot be read as an observed injury. A pregnancy question adds further steps: a study must define the population, measure or estimate relevant exposure and ascertain an outcome with an appropriate comparator. The recovered induction-cooker outcome report uses questionnaire information, rather than measuring each participant’s dose. Linking it to the household exposure model can clarify what information future work needs; it cannot retrospectively create missing individual measurements or demonstrate a causal pathway between cooker use and a birth outcome.

A modelled comparison with a reference value is conditional on the model’s source, geometry and operating assumptions. The induction estimator was developed and checked in Japanese household settings and describes a fixed position; transfer to other homes or changing activity needs further evaluation. The charging simulation has a different limitation: its authors identify field validation and additional source combinations as future work. Parts of its percentage descriptions are also internally inconsistent, so affected numerical claims remain held. These are reasons to report what each model actually represents before discussing compliance. A detailed anatomical illustration can improve the calculation without making it a measured population or proving a health outcome.

For an induction hob, distance is a relationship between the person, the cooking zone and the pan, with alignment and operating conditions retained. Replacing that geometry with one universal separation discards the factors the exposure model was designed to describe. The pregnancy outcome paper does not provide the full pan, position and power information needed to assign each participant the household model’s estimate. Combining the papers therefore helps identify a measurement gap rather than closing it. A better matched comparison would connect the relevant configuration and time at the source to the same people whose outcomes are being assessed, with the model’s validation and uncertainty still visible.

modules.label: Evidence

paragraphs.text: The induction outcome report found weak associations for some preterm-delivery comparisons and no birthweight association in its analyses. Its questionnaire design, follow-up, reporting patterns, repeated testing and residual confounding limit causal interpretation; the authors did not regard the pattern as establishing increased risk. Those results address a human outcome, whereas the household estimator and charger simulation describe exposure. Keeping the streams separate prevents engineering detail from being used as extra clinical evidence or a questionnaire association from validating a dosimetry model. The source pages link the relevant findings and outstanding inputs. No single pooled intermediate-frequency health effect follows from these different sources, configurations and outcomes.

Brief transient fields require a different description from a continuous single-frequency exposure. A pacemaker bench study used an impulse source near an artificial chest model and found that lead geometry changed induced voltage and pacing inhibition. The tested multiple-twist arrangement reduced interference but did not eliminate it under every condition. The source’s statistical annotations also need clarification. This model cannot establish ordinary household risk or a clinically proven implantation technique.

Fertility evidence also includes magnetic fields in the intermediate-frequency range, which should be distinguished from phone and Wi-Fi radiofrequency exposure. Kumari and colleagues exposed male mice in a measured coil system and later examined sperm counts, head shape, movement and reproductive tissue weights. They did not detect an adverse pattern in the count, morphology or weight measures, but found more non-progressive movement and fewer immotile sperm in the higher-field group. Movement without forward progression is not established improved fertilization. The study did not test mating success, and its samples were collected after an unexposed interval, so the result describes selected later indicators rather than every possible reproductive effect.

modules.title: Engineering and health evidence remain separate

overview.text: Intermediate-frequency is a useful navigation category for technologies such as induction cooking, but boundaries and operating components need to be stated. An induction hob, a vehicle charger and a wireless communications link do not become equivalent because all involve electricity. Identify which component, frequency range and operating condition are being assessed.

Recovered material includes an induction-hob exposure model, an observational pregnancy report and a charger simulation. These address engineering conditions, reported use and a modeled component respectively. Keeping those bases separate makes the pages useful without presenting a simulation as clinical evidence.

takeaway: A device can contain several field components. A simulation or measured field does not itself supply a health-risk estimate.

intro: Permanent fields and the static component of MRI, kept separate from time-varying gradients and RF.

modules.label: Properties

paragraphs.text: A static magnetic field has a magnitude and spatial pattern without oscillating over time. A person moving through that pattern encounters a changing field along their path, so a fixed reading at one point and a description of movement answer different questions. MRI adds switched gradients and RF energy for other imaging functions; the scanner’s nominal static-field value cannot describe all three components. This distinction helps interpret an apparent contradiction in a claim about “MRI radiation”: the underlying study may concern movement in the static field, a switched-field effect or RF energy deposition. Identify the component, scanner state, task and body position before comparing its result with another source or outcome.

modules.title: A static component in a mixed system

paragraphs.text: Patients and workers encounter an MRI environment for different purposes and under different patterns of activity. A selected examination is not the same exposure history as repeated assistance, maintenance or movement around equipment. The occupational communication emphasises that fields can be spatially uneven and task dependent, so a stationary measurement may omit an important part of a worker’s experience. ICNIRP’s MRI account also separates patient medical exposure from worker and public contexts. A useful study description therefore states who was observed, which component was assessed, what they were doing and over what period. Worker-oriented context should not be converted into an individual instruction about whether a patient should undergo a particular scan.

Static-field assessment includes direct interactions and indirect questions involving susceptible objects or implanted devices. Those questions differ from RF heating and from the proposed causes of chronic disease. A transient sensory experience reported during high-field work is an endpoint in its own right; it is not interchangeable with a diagnosed neurological condition or tumour. The occupational communication discusses these experiences and the limited longer-term evidence, while synthesising earlier reports rather than newly measuring all of the outcomes it mentions. This gives a useful map of questions, with no basis for transferring a phone-cancer result into an MRI verdict or treating the absence of ionization as a complete safety assessment.

A magnetic-field quantity for a static source cannot be directly compared with an RF absorbed-energy quantity. The purpose of the framework matters as well: patient medical exposure, worker assessment and general public exposure are different contexts. HSE’s employer guidance considers equipment, tasks and workers at particular risk within the UK framework, with more detailed assessment where existing information is insufficient. It does not determine another jurisdiction’s law or establish the suitability of a particular implant for a particular examination. For a reader assessing a numerical claim, the first task is therefore to identify the component, quantity and population to which the original guidance applies; an impressive number without that match is not an interpretable compliance conclusion.

A field map describes how the field varies across a space; a person’s route and movement add a time history to that description. A room label or distance from the scanner can be useful context, but it does not tell the complete story for every task. ICNIRP’s MRI discussion separates movement-related worker questions from patient medical exposure, while implanted-device and object considerations need their own assessment. This is why a generic stand-back distance cannot be derived from a field-category article. The information needed for a specific decision includes the relevant component, actual operating and movement conditions, and device or facility details that a general overview does not supply.

modules.label: Evidence

paragraphs.text: The official sources explain MRI components and assessment contexts, while the occupational position paper synthesises concerns and evidence gaps. They are useful background, with no newly recruited population or complete outcome-by-outcome systematic appraisal supplied by their presence in this library. A source-specific review needs to recover the original studies, identify which field component was examined and distinguish transient symptoms from longer-term disease. The more specific MRI and occupational pages provide those reading paths and show where primary inputs are still missing. An empty clinical comparison is a statement about assessed coverage, rather than a positive or negative finding. Engineering and device studies remain separately identified when they add evidence about a defined physical interaction.

A bench study of iPhone 12 and MagSafe configurations linked a mapped static magnetic field to changes in the operation of tested cardiac implant generators. Relative position and device design mattered, and the observed magnet-mode changes were reversible on removing the phone. Manufacturer-supplied demo devices and programming assistance were part of the experiment. The findings identify a physical device interaction under laboratory conditions, with patient anatomy, newer products and real-world event frequency still unresolved.

modules.title: What the selected sources can establish

overview.text: Static magnetic fields do not alternate with time. ICNIRP describes static magnetic-field quantities and effects. MRI is a prominent strong-field setting, but the scanner also uses switched gradients and radiofrequency energy. A statement about one component should name it.

The recovered occupational position paper addresses workers’ complex and intermittent exposure around MRI and other equipment. It is a synthesis and position statement, rather than a newly recruited health cohort. Its discussion of transient sensory effects does not establish a chronic disease risk for every worker or patient.

takeaway: MRI is a mixed exposure setting. Patient, worker and component-specific questions require different assessments.
title: Static fields
